prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1315; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a left-turn collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck by an oncoming car. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the statements from two independent witnesses. Both describe the other vehicle entering the intersection during the claimant's turn, and both confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Photographs from the scene and the body shop show damage to the driver's side front quarter panel that lines up well with the reported angle of impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 4: The coverage on the policy was in force at the time of loss, and the driver is listed as a named insured on the declarations page. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical summary. The claimed injury is a lower back strain, which fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type.

Entry 6: The other driver's account of the collision matches the claimant's account and the witness statements in its sequence and general details. Our file now contains consistent accounts from all parties.

Entry 7: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account matched the one given at first notice and again in the follow-up call, with no meaningful changes in sequence or detail.

Entry 8: Medical records show a course of treatment that followed a typical pattern, with pain and mobility improving steadily over several weeks. Treatment tapered as the claimant's condition improved, which is consistent with the diagnosis.

Entry 9: The claimant's prior records include a minor strain to the same area many years ago, which the treating provider documented as fully resolved. Nothing in the current treatment suggests a lasting or unrelated condition.

Entry 10: Reviewed the full file with the vehicle damage estimate, witness statements, and medical timeline. Everything supports the reported loss as described, and the claim is being moved to the next stage for evaluation.
